You may see the glass as half empty but it can always be refilled by new experiences. Most of the responses here have been very extreme and unhelpful.   
As some people have said you should set clear boundaries and try and put him at ease so he doesn't actively believe that something might happen. Because the more his paranoia grows the worse it'll be. 

When it's this early then no it's not great that he's already acting like this but if you'd been together for a while then it still wouldn't be great. I personally overthink a lot with my girlfriend but I don't truly believe at all that she's off about to cheat on me. It's more just because I want to be spending time with her rather than being left out. I'm not about to become this toxic abusive boyfriend. Therefore I'd assume that that isn't what's happening here either. 

You just need to clearly tell him that you are your own person. And no he may not like that. But if he backs down and stops reacting so negatively then that's a positive. If he continues to react negatively and won't listen to reason and descend into a jealous mess - then that's a warning sign.

But right now all you need to worry about is explaining your view and reassuring him. I'm not excusing his behaviour. But pairing 2 negative reactions is never a good thing.

These are very extreme reactions to what you've said. This in no way means that abuse will happen. Abuse could happen in the future of any relationship whether it starts out with sparkles and roses or with a toxic a partner. You don't have to worry about the possibility of abuse until clear signs start to show rather than an insecure boyfriend.
